title: Pruning Invalid EXDATE Values When Series DTSTART, RRULE, or RDATE Changes

citations.verbatim_quote: The exception dates, if specified, are used in computing the recurrence set.  The recurrence set is the complete set of recurrence instances for a calendar component.  The recurrence set is generated by considering the initial "DTSTART" property along with the "RRULE", "RDATE", and "EXDATE" properties contained within the recurring component.  The "DTSTART" property defines the first instance in the recurrence set.  The "DTSTART" property value SHOULD match the pattern of the recurrence rule, if specified.  The recurrence set generated with a "DTSTART" property value that doesn't match the pattern of the rule is undefined.  The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties.

Maps recurrence ids (the date-time produced by the recurrence rule) to the overridden properties of the recurrence instance.

   If the recurrence id does not match a date-time from the recurrence rule (or no rule is specified), it is to be treated as an additional occurrence (like an RDATE from iCalendar).  The patch object may often be empty in this case.

   If the patch object defines the "excluded" property of an occurrence to be true, this occurrence is omitted from the final set of recurrences for the calendar object (like an EXDATE from iCalendar).

This defines if this object is an overridden, excluded instance of a recurring JSCalendar object (see Section 4.3.5).  If this property value is true, this calendar object instance MUST be removed from the occurrence expansion.  The absence of this property, or the presence of its default value as false, indicates that this instance MUST be included in the occurrence expansion.

rationale: Under RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.1, EXDATE entries exclude start DATE-TIME or DATE values generated by the component's DTSTART, RRULE, and RDATE properties. In RFC 8984 Sections 4.3.5 and 4.3.6, EXDATE maps to a recurrenceOverrides entry with excluded=true keyed by a recurrence-id produced by the recurrence rule. When a recurring series is edited such that its DTSTART, RRULE, or RDATE changes, previously recorded EXDATE values that no longer correspond to any occurrence generated by (dtstart, rrule, rdate) become stale, dangling exceptions. By store policy, editing a component must prune any EXDATE entry that is no longer in the unexcluded recurrence set of the updated component, and must clear EXDATE completely if the resulting component is non-recurring (rrule is None and rdate is empty).
store_implication: Whenever a component is updated via a store edit: (1) if the resulting component is recurring (rrule is not None or rdate is non-empty), its exdate list MUST be filtered so that only timestamps matching an unexcluded occurrence generated by (dtstart, rrule, rdate) (normalized to the component's timezone or DATE value type) are retained; (2) if the resulting component is non-recurring (rrule is None and rdate is empty, including single-instance overrides), its exdate list MUST be empty ([]).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Moving a daily recurring series (2025-05-23, COUNT=10) with an EXDATE at 2025-05-27 to start on 2025-06-01: 2025-05-27 is no longer generated by the rule and must be removed from the master component's exdate list.

Moving the same daily recurring series (2025-05-23, COUNT=10) with an EXDATE at 2025-05-27 to start on 2025-05-25: 2025-05-27 is still generated by the rule (as the 3rd occurrence) and must be retained in the master component's exdate list.
Converting a recurring series to a non-recurring event (setting rrule=None with empty rdate): any previously recorded EXDATE entries must be cleared completely (exdate=[]).
All-day (DATE) and timezone-aware (DATE-TIME with TZID) EXDATE values must be compared using the updated DTSTART's value type and timezone.

scenarios.name: move_series_past_exdate_prunes_invalid_exdate
scenarios.description: Moving a 3-day recurring series from 2025-05-23 to 2025-06-01 prunes the stale EXDATE on 2025-05-25 because 2025-05-25 is no longer a valid occurrence of the moved series.

audit_notes: Verified +/- 40 lines around all three citations (RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.1 L6738-6751, RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5 L1497-1507, and RFC 8984 Section 4.3.6 L1554-1559).

Confirmed authority STORE_POLICY is accurate: RFC 5545 treats non-matching EXDATEs as a no-op during set subtraction, so actively pruning stale EXDATE values when DTSTART/RRULE/RDATE is edited (and clearing EXDATE when a component becomes non-recurring) is a store hygiene policy.
